relevance_note: One of the 15 enrolled children carries a TNFAIP3 variant with individual-level detail: '1 TNFAIP3 mutation (A20 haploinsufficiency, #15 with BD)'.
method_note: Read the paper manually; a short Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON from my reading and checked every span verbatim. Scope: cohort of 15 children with recurrent aphthous stomatitis; only patient #15 carries a TNFAIP3 variant (Table 2: c.C1135T p.Q379X). The other 14 enrolled patients (STAT1, PTPN22, DNASE1L3 carriers or genetically negative) are out of scope and get no rows. In-scope relatives: the mother of #15 ('also carrying the A20 mutation', affected with BD) and the grandmother of #15 (BD per Table 1 family history 'BD (mother grandmother)'; 'presents complaints similar to the nephew'). The paper does not say whether the grandmother is maternal or paternal, calls #15 her 'nephew', and does not say she was tested, so she has no variant row. Mother's variant row: the variant string is taken from #15's Table 2 row, tied to her by 'STATUS (carrier): HZ(mother)' and 'also carrying the A20 mutation'; her zygosity and inheritance are not stated. Transcript NM_001270508 (printed without a version) comes from Methods and is tied to Table 2 by its legend; '6q23.3' (Chr column) is a cytoband, not recorded as genomic coordinates; the cDNA is printed as 'c.C1135T' and kept verbatim; the authors do not name the variant class, so variant_type is 'not reported'. Table 2 'Inheritance' column ('AD') is the disease mode, not the variant origin. Only in-silico predictions (GERP 5.63, CADD 39, LRT D, MT D) are given for TNFAIP3, no functional assay. Table 1 columns in order: Patient, Sex, Age at enrollment (y), Onset (y), RAS/year, Other clinical characteristics, Laboratory, HLA B51, Pathergy, Familial history, Diagnosis, PED BD, ACR, ACR EULAR, Current therapy, Immunephenotype, IFN score, AA change Gene. Onset '0.3' is in years (P0.3Y). Age at last evaluation is the 'Age at enrollment (y)' value 16; follow-up continued after genetic diagnosis (6 months of adalimumab), so the true age at last evaluation may be higher. Symbols: the legend defines '“-“: negative result' (the table prints an en dash) and 'N normal'; used for Pathergy and Immunephenotype. HLA B51 '–' (negative) is a genetic marker and is not recorded as a phenotype. Judgement calls: the laboratory cell is merged by conversion ('usually normal CRPFecal calprotectin ↑'); 'usually normal CRP' recorded as excluded with the qualifier 'usually normal'. GI checklist item observed from perianal ulcerations and raised fecal calprotectin; skin-lesions item observed from skin abscesses; recurrent fever observed from 'Fever' plus 'further recurrence of ... fever crisis'. is_proband for #15 rests on the Methods' generic use of 'proband' for carriers of causative variants. Vital status 'alive' for #15 rests on his report at the last follow-up. Contradictions: none found for in-scope people. Out of scope: patient #1 is 'F' in Table 1 but called 'he' in the text; the IFN-score text cites 'Table 2' for diagnoses that are in Table 1. Supplementary files are not included in the Markdown (placeholders only).

study_type.span: Subjects consecutively referred to the rheumatology unit of the IRCCS Burlo Garofolo with RAS from January 2015 to January 2020 were enrolled in the study.

is_proband.span: Variants considered to be causative were validated by Sanger Sequencing both in proband and parents, when available.

treatment_summary.value: Glucocorticoids (GC); adalimumab (ADA) started after genetic diagnosis, with no further recurrence of aphthae, abscesses and fever crisis after 6 months of treatment; colchicine refused because of intolerance; no benefit from tonsillectomy
